content.comment_body: Good morning everyone, I'm looking to create an automatic position control solution for a shutter in my machine. The goal is to open and close it in five steps, each step activated by a corresponding switch. I want to use a stepper motor and a rotary encoder for position feedback; however, I'm struggling with the programming aspect. Any guidance or examples would be much appreciated. Thank you!

Hello, Could you share more details? Specifically: 1) Does your stepper motor have an integrated controller that can simply receive up/down signals? If not, you might consider using a regular motor with gears. 2) How will you select the desired position—via a rotary switch or time-based control? Describe your stepping cycle. 3) Using a fast counter input to register encoder pulses can help track position, counting up or down as needed. Be sure to include a counter reset (for example, activate a full closed limit switch and press a reset to set the counter to zero). Please provide this information so I can assist further.

Hello, Generally, combining stepper motors directly with [product_name] is not feasible. Stepper motors need a minimum start/stop frequency, which [product_name] can't supply. The maximum output frequency is determined by the scan time—typically 0.1ms per function block, so for 200 function blocks, the scan time is about 20ms (resulting in roughly 50Hz frequency for transistor outputs). Relay outputs are much slower, maxing at 0.5Hz. Instead, consider using an external stepper drive that can be programmed for your five target positions and speed settings, and trigger these via digital input signals. Some manufacturers offer such stepper drives. Hope this provides clarity.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are trying to automate positional control of a machine's shutter using a stepper motor and encoder feedback. The main obstacle is that [product_name] lacks sufficient output frequency and scan time to directly manage stepper motors for fine motion control. Users are also working through how to structure the logic for feedback and multiple position states.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that [product_name] will offer straightforward, reliable support for stepper motor control and encoder feedback, enabling multi-position operation with user-friendly programming and configuration.
